summary: This is the Thermostat class with its display method rewritten to hand back a String instead of printing it. Returning the text lets a caller decide what to do with it 	est compcompare it against an expected value in a test.

lines.text: The class is the blueprint for a thermostat object; everything that follows lives inside it.

A placeholder standing in for the parts of the class the book has already written, so the page can focus on the one method being changed. Because those pieces are missing, this listing is a fragment for reading rather than a file that compiles on its own.
The return type is now String rather than void, which is the whole point of the change: the method produces a value that the caller receives.

The + operator joins the label to whatever getStatus() reports, and return sends that finished sentence back to the caller. A test can now capture this string and assert on it, which is impossible when a method only prints.
